answer: Latency Ledger Admission. Each identity must answer randomized challenge batches whose send times are drawn from a shared clock; responses are accepted only if their inter-arrival gaps match the node's prior quartz-stamped history within tight tolerance. A slow-drip bridge of new identities cannot inherit an established timing distribution, so each must idle through organic traffic for hours before earning throughput. That wall-clock thread cost multiplies per identity, making bulk fabrication expensive in real waiting time.
